description: Fresh random sample from entire course - independent verification round

worst_3_phrases.english: That is exactly what I'm trying to say, thank you for understand it.
worst_3_phrases.other: Das ist genau das, was ich versuche zu sagen, danke, dass du es verstehst.
worst_3_phrases.reason: GRAMMAR ERROR in English: 'thank you for understand it' is ungrammatical. Should be 'thank you for understanding it'. The German is correct but the English error makes this unusable for teaching.

worst_3_phrases.english: Why she wants to find out what the answer is?
worst_3_phrases.other: Warum will sie herausfinden, was die Antwort ist?
worst_3_phrases.reason: GRAMMAR ERROR in English: Question word order is wrong. Should be 'Why does she want to find out...' not 'Why she wants...'. The German correctly uses verb-second order for questions, but the English is ungrammatical.

worst_3_phrases.english: I think that I want to put it.
worst_3_phrases.other: Ich denke, dass ich es stecken will.
worst_3_phrases.reason: Semantically incomplete: 'put it' requires context (put it WHERE?). 'Stecken' in German is also odd without clarification (stecken implies inserting/sticking into something). Low pedagogical value as a standalone phrase.

systematic_issues.issue: German word order with time/place adverbials
systematic_issues.description: Multiple phrases place time or place adverbials awkwardly at the end of German sentences. In German, time-manner-place order and Satzklammer principles often require these earlier in the sentence.
German requires commas before subordinate clauses introduced by 'wenn', 'dass', etc. Several phrases omit these required commas.
Some phrase fragments lack essential grammatical elements (reflexive pronouns in German, subjects). While acceptable as teaching chunks, they lose precision.

phrases.english: It isn't easy to understand enough different words.
phrases.other: Es ist nicht leicht, genug verschiedene Wörter zu verstehen.
phrases.notes: Both natural, good construction with infinitive clause

phrases.english: He doesn't want to think about it carefully when other people are here.
phrases.other: Er will nicht sorgfältig darüber nachdenken, wenn andere Leute hier sind.
phrases.notes: Correct and natural in both languages, good complexity

phrases.english: You will find something new if you look.
phrases.other: Du wirst etwas Neues finden wenn du suchst.
phrases.notes: Missing comma before 'wenn' in German (subordinate clause)

phrases.english: I can't remember what I wanted to write.
phrases.other: Ich kann mich nicht erinnern, was ich schreiben wollte.
phrases.notes: Good, natural in both languages with proper reflexive

phrases.english: It is not very unusual that people do that differently.
phrases.other: Es ist nicht sehr ungewöhnlich, dass Menschen das anders machen.
phrases.notes: English slightly awkward with double negative construction

phrases.english: Of course you can do that.
phrases.other: Natürlich kannst du das.
phrases.notes: Perfect, natural in both languages

phrases.english: to practise speaking
phrases.other: das Sprechen üben
phrases.notes: Fragment; German uses nominalized infinitive which is a stylistic choice

phrases.english: That old man would help you if he could on Saturday
phrases.other: Dieser alte Mann würde dir helfen, wenn er könnte am Samstag
phrases.notes: Awkward placement of 'am Samstag' at end; should be integrated earlier in German

phrases.english: I want to learn a few words so I feel better.
phrases.other: Ich will ein paar Wörter lernen, damit ich mich besser fühle.
phrases.notes: Good, natural in both languages with purpose clause

phrases.english: remember easily
phrases.other: leicht erinnern
phrases.notes: Fragment; German missing reflexive 'sich' for 'sich erinnern'

phrases.english: Thank you very much, you're doing that very well.
phrases.other: Vielen Dank, du machst das sehr gut.
phrases.notes: Natural in both sides, good conversational phrase

phrases.english: You need to understand that it's not like that as before.
phrases.other: Du musst verstehen dass es nicht so ist wie vorher.
phrases.notes: English awkward 'not like that as before'; German missing comma after 'verstehen'

phrases.english: I don't know how quickly I'm starting to speak English
phrases.other: Ich weiß nicht, wie schnell ich anfange, Englisch zu sprechen
phrases.notes: English semantically odd - 'how quickly I'm starting' is unnatural phrasing

phrases.english: He's just started to watch a film on Sunday
phrases.other: Er hat gerade angefangen, einen Film zu schauen am Sonntag
phrases.notes: German 'am Sonntag' placement awkward; English present perfect with future time marker questionable

phrases.english: My son works for the council, my daughter too
phrases.other: Mein Sohn arbeitet für die Gemeinde, meine Tochter auch
phrases.notes: Good, natural in both languages

phrases.english: What do you need to do now before we can go?
phrases.other: Was musst du jetzt machen, bevor wir gehen können?
phrases.notes: Perfect in both sides, natural question

phrases.english: I want to try to say something in English.
phrases.other: Ich will versuchen etwas auf Englisch zu sagen.
phrases.notes: German missing comma after 'versuchen' before extended infinitive

phrases.english: I think that I want to put it.
phrases.other: Ich denke, dass ich es stecken will.
phrases.notes: Semantically incomplete - 'put it' needs context; 'stecken' odd without destination

phrases.english: I don't know yet when I can come back.
phrases.other: Ich weiß noch nicht, wann ich zurückkommen kann.
phrases.notes: Perfect, natural in both languages

phrases.english: saw a while ago
phrases.other: vor einer Weile gesehen
phrases.notes: Fragment missing subject; acceptable as phrase chunk

phrases.english: I was starting to feel better than last night.
phrases.other: Ich fing an, mich besser zu fühlen als letzte Nacht.
phrases.notes: Good, natural in both with comparison

phrases.english: Can you ask him if he'll be able to help tomorrow afternoon?
phrases.other: Kannst du ihn fragen, ob er helfen kann morgen Nachmittag?
phrases.notes: German word order: 'morgen Nachmittag' should come before or integrated with verb

phrases.english: I can remember
phrases.other: ich kann mich erinnern
phrases.notes: Correct with reflexive; lowercase 'ich' acceptable in fragment

phrases.english: I think, if you can learn that, that would be good
phrases.other: Ich denke, wenn du das lernen könntest, wäre das gut
phrases.notes: English indicative 'can' vs German subjunctive 'könntest' - slight meaning shift

phrases.english: That is exactly what I'm trying to say, thank you for understand it.
phrases.other: Das ist genau das, was ich versuche zu sagen, danke, dass du es verstehst.
phrases.notes: GRAMMAR ERROR: 'for understand' should be 'for understanding'

phrases.english: the film was complete rubbish
phrases.other: der Film war absoluter Müll
phrases.notes: Natural, colloquial in both languages

phrases.english: I think that they're trying to achieve a lot with the work there
phrases.other: Ich denke, dass sie viel erreichen wollen mit der Arbeit dort
phrases.notes: German 'mit der Arbeit dort' placement awkward at end

phrases.english: if he'll be able to help
phrases.other: ob er helfen kann
phrases.notes: English future 'will be able' vs German present 'kann' - acceptable simplification

phrases.english: It's time to speak and not to wait more
phrases.other: Es ist Zeit zu sprechen und nicht mehr zu warten
phrases.notes: English 'wait more' is unnatural - should be 'wait any longer'

phrases.english: Why she wants to find out what the answer is?
phrases.other: Warum will sie herausfinden, was die Antwort ist?
phrases.notes: GRAMMAR ERROR: Should be 'Why does she want' - incorrect question word order

phrases.english: That's not very helpful if you don't tell me what you want
phrases.other: Das ist nicht sehr hilfreich, wenn du mir nicht sagst, was du willst
phrases.notes: Natural in both languages

phrases.english: But I have to take my mother to the doctor tomorrow morning
phrases.other: Aber ich muss meine Mutter zum Arzt bringen morgen früh
phrases.notes: German 'morgen früh' placement awkward at end

phrases.english: I'm ready to keep on doing this when you're ready
phrases.other: Ich bin bereit damit weiterzumachen, wenn du bereit bist
phrases.notes: Good translation in both

phrases.english: I'm afraid I have to go now, my mother is waiting
phrases.other: Tut mir leid, ich muss jetzt gehen, meine Mutter wartet
phrases.notes: 'I'm afraid' to 'Tut mir leid' is reasonable cultural equivalent

phrases.english: She wants to read everything before she starts to speak.
phrases.other: Sie will alles lesen, bevor sie anfängt zu sprechen.
phrases.notes: Good in both languages

phrases.english: He wants to speak English tomorrow.
phrases.other: Er will morgen Englisch sprechen.
phrases.notes: Perfect, natural in both languages

phrases.english: That's a good idea but I am not sure.
phrases.other: Das ist eine gute Idee, aber ich bin mir nicht sicher.
phrases.notes: Good in both languages

phrases.english: ask for the same thing to eat
phrases.other: das Gleiche zum Essen bestellen
phrases.notes: 'ask for' to 'bestellen' is more specific but reasonable in context

phrases.english: He wants to learn her name quickly.
phrases.other: Er will schnell ihren Namen lernen.
phrases.notes: Natural in both languages

phrases.english: was hoping would happen
phrases.other: mir erhofft hatte
phrases.notes: Fragment with mismatch; German changes to reflexive construction

phrases.english: They are people I don't know, but want to meet
phrases.other: Das sind Leute, die ich nicht kenne, aber kennenlernen will
phrases.notes: Good, natural in both languages

phrases.english: The man was too busy, he had no time for me there
phrases.other: Der Mann war zu beschäftigt, er hatte keine Zeit für mich dort
phrases.notes: Natural in both languages

phrases.english: I wanted to find the money on the table, but it was not there
phrases.other: Ich wollte das Geld finden auf dem Tisch, aber es war nicht da
phrases.notes: German 'auf dem Tisch' placement awkward after infinitive

phrases.english: where do you want to do that
phrases.other: wo willst du das machen
phrases.notes: Natural in both languages

phrases.english: I know an old man who wants to work with you there
phrases.other: Ich kenne einen alten Mann, der mit dir arbeiten will dort
phrases.notes: German 'dort' placement awkward at end

phrases.english: Have you heard that he's trying to find the money?
phrases.other: Hast du gehört, dass er versucht, das Geld zu finden?
phrases.notes: Good in both languages

phrases.english: I'm not sure if it will work, but we can try it
phrases.other: Ich bin mir nicht sicher, ob es funktionieren wird, aber wir können es versuchen
phrases.notes: Good in both languages

phrases.english: I understand now what you said earlier, and I'm grateful to you.
phrases.other: Ich verstehe jetzt, was du vorhin meintest, und ich bin dir dankbar.
phrases.notes: Excellent, natural in both languages

phrases.english: Nobody wanted to tell me what the problem was in the office there
phrases.other: Niemand wollte mir sagen, was das Problem war im Büro dort
phrases.notes: German 'im Büro dort' awkward placement at end

phrases.english: what's going to happen tomorrow
phrases.other: was morgen passieren wird
phrases.notes: Perfect, natural in both languages
